title: Personal Finance: Final Assessment
description: A final assessment covering the key ideas from all three lessons. Reach the passing score to complete the course.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not reviewed or approved by a human (admin); do not give to students.

Comprehensive audit: q3 distractors made specific so the key is not the only numeric choice, and the explanation's 'June' corrected to 12 months; q4 uses 'interest rate' for a deposit; q7 replaced (redundant inflation-risk recall) with a credit card minimum-payment calculation; q8 percent-entry instruction and difficulty set to intermediate; q9 choices made parallel with two finance-related targets; q10 choices made parallel so the key is not the only two-part choice. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

passing.note: Proposed: 7 of 10 questions (70%). Not approved by a teacher (admin); completion is not recognized until approved.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Chris earns $3,000 a month in gross pay, and deductions take 18% of it. Chris plans to save 20% of net (take-home) income. How many dollars a month will Chris save? (Enter a number only.)
Hypothetical example: Dana wants to free up $50 in next month's budget. Which change can she most likely make the fastest?

choices.text: Move to an apartment with cheaper rent
Change the terms of her yearly phone contract
Spend less on eating out and entertainment
Switch to a car loan with lower payments

questions.prompt: Which of these is the best example of a SMART financial goal?

choices.text: Save $900 for a laptop in 12 months by setting aside $75 a month
Save as much as I can for a laptop over the next 12 months
Save $900 for a laptop someday by cutting back on extras
Save $900 for a laptop in 12 months by setting aside $25 a month

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Maya opens a savings account with $1,500. It pays a 4.8% interest rate (stated per year), compounded monthly, and she makes no other deposits or withdrawals for one year. How much is in the account at the end of the year? Round to the nearest cent, and round only at the final step. (Enter a number only.)
Hypothetical example: Your savings account pays 2% a year, and prices rise 3% over the same year. What happens to the purchasing power of your savings?

choices.text: It rises by about 2%, because the account balance grows
It stays the same, because interest is paid on the balance
It rises by about 5%, the sum of interest and inflation
It falls by about 1%, because prices rise faster than the balance

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Loan X and Loan Y are each $5,000 for three years at the same 8% interest rate. Loan Y also charges a $150 fee to set up the loan. If the disclosed APR includes this fee, how do the two loans compare?

choices.text: Both APRs are 8%, because the interest rates are equal
Loan Y has the higher APR, because it costs more in total
Loan X has the higher APR, because Y's fee lowers its rate
Loan Y has the lower APR, because fees are paid up front

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Sam has a $1,000 credit card balance. The card charges 2% interest per month on the balance, and Sam makes no new purchases. Each month, interest is added first, and then Sam pays $25. What is the balance after 2 months, in dollars? Round to the nearest cent, and round only at the final step. (Enter a number only.)

Hypothetical example: A lender wants an expected return of 3% on one-year loans. It expects 5% of borrowers to default and repay nothing. Using (1 + i)(1 − default share) = 1 + target return, what interest rate i must it charge, in percent? Round to two decimal places. (Enter a number only; for example, enter 25 for 25%.)

Hypothetical example: A program in Country V helps rural households, many with no bank account, open mobile money accounts linked to a savings feature and simple insurance. Which SDG target does this most directly support?

choices.text: Target 8.3, support for small firms, including access to finance
Target 1.1, ending extreme poverty for all people everywhere
Target 8.5, decent work and equal pay for all workers
Target 1.4, equal access to resources, including financial services

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A friend says, "Fund Z returned 15% a year for the last three years, so it will keep doing that. Put your emergency fund in it." What is the best response?

choices.text: Agree, because three good years show that its return is reliable
Agree, as long as the fund charges lower fees than a savings account
Disagree, because emergency money should stay stable and easy to reach
Disagree, because funds with high past returns tend to lose money next
